title: RBAC v2 role matrix + evidence automation playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working playbook captures the RBAC v2 role matrix, policy templates, and environment-by-environment access rules for Redwood Inference. It ties RBAC to audit log schema, evidence automation recipes, and SIEM export conventions. This is a living doc: use it for reviews, audits, and for onboarding Dedicated/Private deployments.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Adopt a small set of composable roles (Viewer, Operator, Model-Publisher, Billing-Reader, Admin) + environment-scoped grant policies.
- Use attribute-based constraints for private/dedicated resources (customer_id, region, infra_zone).
- Emit a normalized JSON audit record for every privileged action; feed to SIEM via Kafka + syslog shippers.
- Evidence automation collects snapshots for rollouts, canary configs, and RBAC changes; defaults to 90-day evidence retention for standard customers, adjustable per contract.

1) RBAC v2 role matrix (conceptual)
- Roles are composable and permission-based, not persona-based. Roles can be assigned at three scopes: global (org), account (customer), resource (model, deployment).
- Primitive permissions (examples): read:tokens, create:deploy, update:deploy, rollback:deploy, list:models, publish:model, read:billing, manage:iam, view:audit, export:audit.

Role definitions (recommended baseline):
- Viewer
  - Permissions: view:audit (limited to allowed scopes), list:models, read:tokens (masked), view:metrics
  - Typical assignees: auditors, compliance reviewers

- Operator
  - Permissions: create:deploy, update:deploy, rollback:deploy, list:models, view:metrics, view:audit
  - Constraints: cannot publish new model versions or change RBAC

- Model-Publisher
  - Permissions: publish:model, update:model-metadata, create:deploy (restricted), view:audit
  - Constraints: publish scoped to customer-managed repositories for Private/Dedicated; hosted catalog uses curated publishing flow

- Billing-Reader
  - Permissions: read:billing, view:cost-metrics
  - Constraints: read-only, no export of PII, export of aggregated cost data only

- Admin
  - Permissions: manage:iam, manage:policy, export:audit, admin:all
  - Constraints: emergency-only for cross-account changes; require 2-person approval for global scope

2) Environment-by-environment rules (hosted | dedicated | private)
- Hosted (default Redwood API):
  - RBAC supports org-scoped roles for Redwood accounts.
  - Non-customer-managed resources (e.g., Redwood's shared model catalog) are governed by product-level policy: only Model-Publisher and Admin can add to hosted catalog.
  - Operators can deploy to dedicated pools only if assigned both Operator role and specific resource grant for the dedicated pool.
  - Evidence retention defaults: audit logs 365 days, artifacts (release tags) 180 days.

- Dedicated (customer reserved capacity):
  - Access is controlled by customer_id tag. Roles can be bound to Redwood identities or customer SSO groups via SCIM.
  - Operators and Model-Publishers must have explicit "pool-grant" for each GPU pool.
  - Admin-level operations (e.g., scale, kernel upgrades) require an ops runbook entry + a property change audit event.
  - Evidence retention: per-contract; default 365 days for audit; evidence automation exports to customer S3/KMS if requested as part of contract.

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Customers manage primary IAM and optionally federate to Redwood via SAML/OIDC.
  - RBAC policies are translated and enforced locally via the Redwood Private agent.
  - Additional attribute required: environment_owner (customer-owned) and isolation_level (air-gapped / connected).
  - For air-gapped: SIEM export is file-based bundle of UTF-8 JSON logs signed with HSM key; for connected: real-time Kafka + TLS pipeline.
  - Evidence retention: customer-controlled; Redwood recommends 1 year for infra events and 3 years for security-sensitive events depending on compliance regime.

3) Policy templates (examples)
- Minimal least-privilege publish policy (JSON pseudo-template):
  - "Effect: Allow" on actions: publish:model; resource: "arn:redwood:catalog:${region}:${org}:${modelId}"; Condition: StringEquals: {"requester.role":"Model-Publisher"} ; Condition: ArnLike: {"resource.customer_id":"${customer_id}"}

- Pool operator policy:
  - Allow: create:deploy, update:deploy on resource: "arn:redwood:pool:${region}:${poolId}" with Condition: StringEquals: {"requester.roles":"Operator"} and Bool: {"requester.mfa":"true"}

(These templates are intentionally compact; source-of-truth is infra repo PRs.)

4) Audit log schema (normalized event model)
- Basic required fields for each privileged event (always present):
  - event_id: UUID
  - timestamp: ISO8601
  - requester_id: principal id (redwood:user:...)
  - requester_type: human|service
  - requester_claims: list (roles, groups, attrs)
  - action: canonical action name (e.g., publish:model, update:rbac)
  - resource: canonical resource ARN
  - outcome: success|failure|partial
  - request_context: {ip, region, user_agent} (flattened key strings in JSON)
  - change_set: brief delta (if config change), stringified JSON patch when available
  - evidence_refs: list of evidence artifact ids (snapshot ids, S3 paths)
  - trace_id: correlation id

- Transport/encoding notes:
  - Primary wire format = compact JSON per-line (ndjson). Field names are snake_case.
  - For SIEM ingestion include an "event_type" tag: security|ops|billing to make indexing cheaper.

5) SIEM export patterns
- Real-time streaming (recommended for Hosted + Dedicated):
  - Push to internal Kafka topic redwood.audit.ndjson, consumers (log-shipper) fanout to SIEMs: Splunk HTTP Event Collector, Datadog Logs, Sumo Logic, or customer Kafka cluster (Dedicated).
  - TLS mutual auth between producers and SIEM endpoints.

- Batch export (Private / air-gapped):
  - Bundle ndjson files daily, sign with HSM key, and upload to the customer-specified location (S3, scp to internal host). Include a manifest.json with offsets and checksums.

- Mapping guidance for SIEM parsers:
  - Map action -> event.action, outcome->event.outcome, requester_id->user.id, resource ARN fields to custom fields (resource.type/resource.id).

6) Evidence automation (playbook)
- Triggers for evidence capture:
  - RBAC changes (create/update/delete policy or role assignment) -> capture current role-assignment snapshot + diff + approver chain
  - Production rollout (canary/100%) -> capture canary config, request logs for first 5 minutes, KV cache warm-up metrics, policy attached to deployment
  - Emergency access (break-glass) -> capture who, justification, duration, and all actions performed during emergency window

- Evidence artifacts (what we collect):
  - snapshot: role-assignments.json (flattened list)
  - config: deployment-config.yml
  - audit_extract.ndjson (events matching trace_id or time window)
  - verification: smoke-test results + perf sample metrics
  - signature: signed_manifest.json

- Automation mechanics:
  - On trigger, orchestration job runs on the control plane and writes artifacts to the evidence bucket (encrypted with customer KMS if requested).
  - Jobs create a unique evidence_id and attach it to the corresponding audit events via evidence_refs.
  - Retention & TTL enforced by policy; evidence deletion is a two-step process (mark_for_deletion -> audit-approved purge).

7) Operational controls and approvals
- RBAC changes to global Admin role require 2 approvals: one security approver + one engineering approver. Approvals must be recorded as part of the evidence artifact.
- Emergency access: require a post-factum 3-day review and produce a remediation ticket in Jira (SEC-EMERGENCY-xxx).

8) Testing and validation
- Periodic (quarterly) policy compliance scans: run least-privilege analyzer and flag roles with >90% permissiveness beyond job needs.
- SIEM ingest tests: simulate ndjson events and validate parser mapping in staging; baseline number of fields and event types.

9) Open questions / items to resolve
- Multi-tenant hosted: what is the explicit masking policy for tokens when a Viewer is granted cross-customer read? (TODO: define masking algorithm)
- Evidence retention SLAs for enterprise customers — convert language into contract clauses (Legal to draft).
- Automated remediation: should we auto-disable risky role bindings flagged by analyzer or just file tickets? (Ops preference: file ticket + notify).

Appendix A: Example RBAC change audit record (ndjson)
{
  "event_id": "uuid-1234",
  "timestamp": "2024-12-12T15:42:01Z",
  "requester_id": "redwood:user:priya.desai",
  "requester_type": "human",
  "requester_claims": ["Admin", "sso:eng-core"],
  "action": "update:role-assignment",
  "resource": "arn:redwood:iam::org:role:Admin",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_context": "ip=34.210.12.5 region=us-west-2 ua=CLI/1.2",
  "change_set": "added: user redwood:user:igor.petrov to Admin",
  "evidence_refs": ["evidence:20241212-9876"],
  "trace_id": "trace-7b9f"
}

Notes: keep this doc short — move formal policy JSONs and infra hooks to the infra repo and link there. Use this playbook for audits, tabletop exercises, and handoffs to Dedicated/Private onboarding engineers.

Unresolved: assign owner for "masking policy" (recommended: Evan Brooks) and add Legal to retention policy finalization.

End of playbook.
